subject: Isolation expectations & evidence request — Dedicated vs Private VPC
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintrust.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintrust.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Isolation requirements and evidence needed (recap + next steps)

Hi Olivia / Samir — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on FT-4891.

Recap of what you called out:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for PII and transaction data. Evaluating Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC / on-prem.
- Controls requested: encryption at rest and in transit, ability to restrict all network egress, disable shared caching/prefixing, and customer-managed key support (KMS/HSM).
- Evidence requested from security: SOC 2 Type II, pen-test summary, sample network diagrams / port/subnet list, and configuration checklist.
- Expected workload: approx 10 TPS steady-state, occasional spikes to 40 TPS for batch runs.

Questions we need clarified from your side before the SecOps call:
1) Is running in your AWS account (Private VPC) a hard requirement, or will a Redwood-managed Dedicated pool with VPC peering be acceptable?
2) Do you require on-prem (air-gapped) options or just VPC isolation in the cloud?
3) Any specific regulator-driven retention/erasure timelines we should bake into the proposal?

Attachments I’m sending with this email: redwood_privacy_one-pager.pdf and redwood_dedicated_config_summary.pdf — short reads covering the two deployment modes.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll get Neha (solutions engineering) to join a 30-min technical call with your SecOps team to walk the config differences (Dedicated vs Private VPC) and hand off the more detailed checklist.
- Samir: if you can share your network checklist (or we can use the attached template), we’ll prepare a tailored diagram and a short evidence pack (SOC2 + pen test summary + encryption details).

Availability: Neha and I are available Wed/Thu morning PST this week. Please suggest a 30-min slot.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_privacy_one-pager.pdf (1 page), redwood_dedicated_config_summary.pdf (2 pages)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintrust.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Isolation requirements and evidence needed (recap + next steps)

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from SecOps to help prep the call:  

- Our baseline: we prefer customer-owned networking (Private VPC) where the control plane is accessible only over private links. Redwood-managed Dedicated is acceptable only if data-at-rest and secondary storage can be isolated to our tenancy and we can enforce egress rules strictly.
- We need confirmation whether Redwood uses any shared object storage for model artifacts or KV cache that would store customer data on multi-tenant storage. If so, can that be disabled or restricted to per-tenant volumes?
- Evidence list: SOC 2 Type II report (latest), summary of external penetration test (date + scope), high-level network diagram showing control plane / data plane boundaries, list of required ports/subnets, and KMS model (customer-managed keys required ideally).
- Compliance note: we’re subject to state financial regulations that require either customer-managed key rotation or an auditable HSM solution.

I attached our initial network checklist (ft_network_checklist.xlsx) — fill in any redwood fields you can before the call. Also, include a short note on timelines: how long to provision Dedicated vs Private VPC and what the expected downtime/maintenance windows look like.

Samir Patel
Security Architect, FinTrust
samir.patel@fintrust.com

Attachment: ft_network_checklist.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintrust.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintrust.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Isolation requirements and evidence needed (recap + next steps)

Samir — great list, thanks. Quick responses inline and proposed prep for the SecOps call.

1) Shared storage / KV cache: by default our hosted runtime uses per-tenant volumes for persistent artifacts; shared KV cache can be disabled per-customer. For Dedicated we can ensure model artifacts and any cached state live on single-tenant volumes. For Private VPC we run in your account (no shared storage). I’ll confirm the exact mount/volume types in the call.

2) Evidence pack we can provide before the call: latest SOC 2 Type II report (redacted where needed), an executive summary of our most recent external pentest, and a sample network diagram showing control plane endpoints and data plane egress flows. We’ll also provide the ports/subnets table you attached (filled).

3) KMS / keys: we support customer-managed KMS in both Dedicated and Private VPC modes. For Private VPC you can bring your own CMK (AWS KMS) or an HSM; for Dedicated we can accept customer-managed keys (we can show the flow and where keys are used).

4) Timelines: typical provisioning estimate — Dedicated: 2–4 weeks (configuration + validation); Private VPC: 6–8 weeks (network onboarding, mutual TLS, and any change windows). These are conservative estimates; Neha will give a tighter RACI on the call.

Proposed prep for SecOps call:
- Neha (solutions engineering) will walk the attached dedicated_config_summary and the checklist you provided.
- Marcus will share SOC2 + pen-test summary + sample network diagram ahead of the call.

Please pick one of these 30-min slots (PST): Wed 11/4 09:00–09:30, Wed 11/4 11:00–11:30, Thu 11/5 08:30–09:00. If none work, propose alternatives.

Thanks — we’ll aim to get the evidence pack uploaded to the shared Drive link and a filled checklist before the meeting.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_privacy_one-pager.pdf (1 page), redwood_dedicated_config_summary.pdf (2 pages)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintrust.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@fintrust.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Isolation requirements and evidence needed (recap + next steps)

Marcus — Wed 11/4 11:00–11:30 PST works for us.

Two small pre-call asks:
- Please include the ports/subnets spreadsheet completed for the Private VPC option (we’ll use it to open tickets).
- Short note on how key rotation is handled if we bring our own KMS (who can rotate, audit trails, and whether Redwood ever has access to plaintext).

If you can drop those into the HubSpot deal and the Drive folder before 11:00 PST Wed, that’d be ideal.

Samir
